newsitem.title: USA: Atlantic Gulf Q1 hurt by fewer asset sales.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Gulf Q1 hurt by fewer asset sales.

text.p: Atlantic Gulf Communities Corp on Wednesday said its first-quarter revenues dropped because of lower sales of predecessor assets and subdivision home sites.
As of March 31, the real estate developer had 569 subdivision home sites under contract for about $12.6 million. The contracts are expected to close in 1997, the company said in a statement.
Also, there were pending predecessor tract sales of $18 million expected to close in 1997.
A company representative was not immediately available for comment regarding the term predecessor assets and as it applies to Atlantic Gulf.
An Atlantic Gulf spokesman later said predecessor assets are those that were once held by General Development Corp, which went bankrupt in 1989 and was reorganized into Altantic Gulf in 1992.
Proceeds from those property sales are being used to repay debt, the spokesman said.
